title: The array-of-records control document, taken through reconstruct() instead of reconstructToMap()
rationale: Byte-identical avsc and input to avro-array-of-records-control, which is published LOSSLESS. The ONLY difference between the two rows is which sibling entry point is called. That makes the split visible as a single-variable experiment rather than as two unrelated observations, and it is the row a consumer who read the control and then wrote an Avro file needs to see.
catchesBugClass: The executor-side failure specifically: two elements, both wrong, so a fix that repairs only element 0 - the last-element-repeat family this corpus already documents - still fails. Paired with the minimal reproducer it also catches a 'fix' that special-cases arrays and leaves plain nested records broken.
cannotCatch: An empty array and a null element are not exercised; avro-array-of-records-null-element-annihilates-array already shows those go wrong upstream of reconstruct(), so this row cannot tell you whether reconstruct() adds a second failure on top. It also cannot catch arrays of arrays or arrays of unions.

predicted.detail: orders is set as an ArrayList<LinkedHashMap>; validate fails on the element type and the binary encode throws. avroDoc equals avroBaseline as in the minimal reproducer, so the conjunction is again load-bearing.
